resources.string: Reviewers measure the same headphones differently. Play some music and switch between them. They play at about the same loudness as your current sound.
Could not download these measurements. Check your connection and try again.
This phone doesn\'t allow the extra bands these need, so they have no effect here.
Turns a range of frequencies down only while it\'s too loud, so the rest of the time your sound is untouched. A normal EQ cut would dull it all the time. Saved with each preset.
Holds back sharp treble, such as sibilance and cymbals, around 4 to 9 kHz, when it gets loud. Too much can make music sound dull, so use as little as helps.
Holds back deep bass below about 110 Hz when it surges, so heavy tracks stay under control without thinning out the rest.
Paste a code someone shared with you. It\'s added as a new preset, and your others are kept.

Shows the level of each frequency behind the curve, only while this screen is open. Android requires microphone permission for this, but only levels of playing audio are read. The lowest bands look coarse.

Loads the assigned preset whenever this output connects. If a per-app preset also applies, the latest change wins: connecting headphones loads the output\'s preset, and a different app starting to play loads that app\'s.

Saves your presets, your shapes, output and per-app choices, and favourites to a file. Ear correction and hearing checks are included. Other settings that aren\'t part of a preset, such as balance and night mode, aren\'t.
Shifts sound towards the left or right ear. Useful if one side sounds quieter to you.
Raises or lowers the low end, up to the frequency set below it. This is saved with the preset when you save or update it.
Battery optimisation can stop apps in the background. Allowing background use helps keep the EQ running when the phone is locked.
Hides which sound is which until you\'ve chosen, in a random order, so a name can\'t sway you. Your choice is revealed at the end.
Switch instantly between two presets, or a preset and your current sound, at about the same loudness. Nothing changes unless you choose one.
How quickly it reacts once a sound crosses the threshold. Slower values let the start of drum hits through, which keeps them punchy.
Turn this off to leave this range of frequencies untouched.

Brings loud and quiet parts closer together, separately for bass, mids and treble. Start from a style and adjust by ear. Night mode takes over while it\'s on, and this replaces the volume leveller. It\'s saved with each preset.
The frequency where one band ends and the next begins.
How gradually compression starts around the threshold. Higher values are smoother and less noticeable.
Turns this band back up afterwards, to make up for the level that compression took away.
How strongly levels above the threshold are turned down. At 4 : 1, going 4 dB over the threshold only comes out 1 dB over. Around 2 : 1 is subtle.
How quickly it lets go afterwards. Very short values can make the sound flutter, and long values make it steadier.
Anything louder than this gets turned down. Lower values compress more of the music. Phone volume doesn\'t change this, because it happens before the volume control.

How much of this preset\'s own filters to apply, such as a headphone correction. 100% is as designed, and 0% removes them while keeping your faders and tone. If a sound seems muted or dull, try turning this down.
A technical record of the last crash, kept only on this phone. You choose whether to share it, and deleting it removes it.
Copies technical details about your phone and the audio engine, for reporting a problem. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you paste it somewhere.

A separate EQ for each ear, from the hearing check. It closes half of the gap between your ears at each frequency, and stays on when you change preset. A check also measures the headphones, so each pair keeps its own, which turns on when they connect. Fit can affect the result, so repeat the check if it sounds off. Each pair\'s latest check is kept, so you can turn this on later or again after removing it.

Global covers every app Android allows, and Auto tries it first. If the EQ makes no difference, try Per app, which only covers players that announce their audio. Those players must start after Eigentone.

Both shape the same sound and work together. Graphic gives you fixed faders, which is the quick way. Parametric lets you choose each filter\'s exact frequency and width, which suits fixing a specific problem.
Saves this preset\'s sound as a GraphicEQ text file, which AutoEq-compatible apps and Equalizer APO can read. Surround and settings outside the preset aren\'t included.

Saves this preset\'s filters as a ParametricEQ text file, for AutoEq-compatible apps and Equalizer APO. It only works for presets made of filters, because faders and imported curves can\'t be written that way.
Star the presets you switch between. The notification\'s Next preset button moves through your starred presets, or all of them if none are starred.
Turns this one filter off without deleting it, so you can hear what it was doing.
Bell changes a range around one frequency. Shelves change everything below or above it. High pass removes what\'s below it, and low pass removes what\'s above it.
Searches AutoEq\'s published correction profiles and adds the one you pick. It needs internet access. Measurements are a starting point, and your ears and fit still matter.
A short listening test. You pick your favourite of two versions a few times, and Eigentone builds a preset from your answers. Nothing is kept unless you save it.
The pitch this filter works on. Lower numbers are bass, and higher numbers are treble.
How much this filter boosts or cuts, in decibels. Around 3 dB is a clear but gentle change.
More bands allow finer changes. 10 is quickest, and 31 is the most precise but harder to set by finger. Switching keeps your curve\'s overall shape.
Fixed faders from deep bass to high treble. Drag a fader, or sweep your finger across to draw a curve. The sound follows the faders directly, and it\'s saved with the preset.
Ready-made curves to start from. Tap one, then adjust it to taste. It replaces the current faders, and your preset\'s headphone correction stays underneath, so it adds to that.
Softens sharp steps between neighbouring faders, which often sounds more natural. Tap it again for a stronger effect.
A few short tips, in the order that makes the most difference.
Boosting can push audio past its maximum and cause distortion. This turns the level down by your largest boost, so the sound may get quieter as you add EQ.
Plays quiet tones in each ear to build a gentle curve for what you hear least well, and can correct each ear separately. It takes about 3 minutes. It isn\'t a medical test.
Adds a preset from an AutoEq or Equalizer APO file, either ParametricEQ or GraphicEQ. A GraphicEQ file keeps every point, with no rounding to faders.
Slowly evens out loud and quiet passages, which helps when apps and tracks differ in level. Higher values sound flatter. Night mode and the compressor take priority while they\'re on.
A safety net that holds back sudden peaks so they don\'t distort. It rarely needs turning off.
The level where the limiter starts working. Keep it near -1 dB. Much lower values make loud parts quieter and flatter.
Ears hear less bass and treble at low volume, so this adds more of both as you turn the volume down. It\'s a simplified curve, not a measured one.
How much bass and treble are added at low volume. Lower it if quiet listening sounds too boomy.
Reduces processing delay for games and video, but bass control gets less precise.
Louder usually sounds better, which makes comparisons unfair. This keeps Bypass at about the same loudness, so you\'re comparing tone. The match is an estimate.
Brings quiet and loud parts closer together, so you can hear details at low volume without sudden loud moments. High values can make music sound flatter.
How strong night mode is during the scheduled hours.
Turns night mode on at the times you choose. It only works while Eigentone is running, and it won\'t lower a stronger setting you\'ve chosen above.
The time night mode turns off. It can be after midnight.
The time night mode turns on.

Earbuds can sound different in each mode, so each can have its own preset. Eigentone can\'t read the mode from your earbuds, so set it here to match. A mode with no preset uses this output\'s main one.
Choose the preset that loads for what\'s connected now, such as your earbuds or the phone speaker.

Plays notes and asks whether each stands out from those beside it. It asks twice about anything you flag, narrows it down, then suggests filters you can compare with music before keeping. It finds what your ears notice, and isn\'t a measurement.

Android only reveals which app is playing to apps with notification access. Eigentone ignores your notifications and only checks the playing app, and that stays on your phone. Without it, everything else still works.

Loads a preset when a chosen app starts playing, such as one sound for Spotify and another for YouTube. If an output preset also applies, the latest change wins: a different app starting to play loads that app\'s preset, and connecting headphones loads the output\'s.

The switch turns Eigentone on or off, and it keeps running in the background until you turn it off. Bypass temporarily removes the EQ and effects so you can compare the sound. It doesn\'t change your settings.
Raises or lowers the overall level before the EQ. It\'s saved with the preset, so changing it marks the preset as edited.
How narrow the filter is. Low values change a wide range and sound gentle. High values target a small range, which suits fixing one problem frequency.
Returns to Flat and clears night mode, balance, ear correction, loudness and level settings. Your saved presets, hearing checks and output choices are kept.
Adds presets, your shapes, per-app choices, ear correction and hearing checks from a backup file. Anything with the same identity is replaced, and the rest is kept.
Saves the current sound as a new preset of your own: filters, graphic EQ, tone, surround, compressor and preamp.
How strongly the shape is applied. 100% is as designed, lower is more subtle, and higher is stronger. Double-tap to return to 100%.

Search by genre, instrument, situation or problem, or filter by what a curve does, such as More bass. Tap a shape to hear it on your music, matched in loudness so the comparison is fair, and nothing is kept until you choose Use this. The level may change slightly when you do. Shapes marked with a source come from published data, such as equal-loudness contours and Harman\'s listening tests. The rest are designed starting points, not measurements. Thumbnails run from 20 Hz on the left to 20 kHz on the right.
Replace swaps your faders for this shape. Add puts it on top of your current faders, so you can layer shapes, such as a genre plus a fix for something too harsh.
Creates a text code holding this whole sound, which you can send to someone. It contains EQ settings only, and nothing about you.
Turns the EQ back on after a phone restart or app update, if it was on before.
The players Eigentone is processing in Per app mode.
How finely your curve is reproduced. More is more accurate, and 128 is the most Eigentone asks for.
Whether Eigentone controls the effect. If another audio app takes over, Eigentone\'s settings may stop applying.
Which audio route is in use. Global applies to all apps it can reach, and Per app applies to individual players.
Where Eigentone thinks audio is going. This decides which preset loads.
Eigentone reads its settings back from Android to confirm they were applied. All bands should match, such as 128/128.

How many times Eigentone has rebuilt the effect after losing it since it last started, such as when Android\'s audio system restarts. Occasional repairs are fine, but a rising number suggests a problem on this phone.
Whether the audio effect is currently loaded.

Makes the sound feel wider by leaning small frequency ranges left and right in turn, while keeping bass centred. It\'s subtle by design, with no head tracking or surround channels. Higher values can make vocals feel less centred. This is saved with the preset.

More or less of everything this preset does to the tone. 100% is as saved, 0% is flat, and 150% exaggerates it. An easy way to soften a sound that\'s too much. Surround, preamp and cut-off filters aren\'t affected.

Makes the sound feel wider than your head, using your phone\'s own effect. It doesn\'t track head movement or create real surround channels. Higher values can make vocals feel less centred. This is saved with the preset.

Plays a tone that climbs through the frequencies. Mark where it jumps out or nearly disappears, and Eigentone adds narrow filters there. It finds what your ears notice, and isn\'t a measurement. Sweeps also reveal rattles and resonances that music can hide. If a moving tone is hard to judge, pause and compare the spot with nearby notes.
Off lets you hear the headphones without your EQ, which is best for finding problems. On lets you check how your sound handles them, including filters you\'ve added.
How loud the tone is, before your phone\'s volume. It can\'t go above a set limit, so it stays gentle at a normal volume.

Swaps Eigentone\'s stereo width for the effect built into your phone. It\'s stronger, but it varies by phone and can colour the sound. Android has deprecated it, so a future update could remove it. If your phone refuses it, stereo width takes over.
Raises or lowers everything above about 8 kHz. This is saved with the preset when you save or update it.
Adds or removes low end on top of the correction.
Adjusts this preset\'s correction to taste, with a before and after. Corrections aim for neutral, which isn\'t always what sounds best to you.
Adds or removes brightness on top of the correction.
Replaces your saved preset with the edits you\'ve just made.
Raises or lowers the range around 2.5 kHz, where voices and many instruments are easiest to pick out. This is saved with the preset.
A correction aims for a neutral sound, which isn\'t always what you\'ll enjoy. Use less of it, or add some bass or treble back.
Guided: answer a few questions, and it finds peaks and dips
A headphone correction evens out your model\'s sound first, so your choices start from a balanced base. You\'ll compare the result with your current sound at the end.
A tone climbs from deep bass to high treble. It should stay about equally loud, so mark anywhere it jumps out or nearly disappears. Keep your volume low, and stop if it\'s ever uncomfortable.
After you hear one, the next is quieter, so it\'s normal for tones to become very faint or vanish. Answer honestly rather than guessing.
Android lists this under notification access. Eigentone only checks which app is playing.
Battery optimisation may stop the EQ when locked.
Builds a curve for how you hear
Bypass is on, so you won\'t hear the changes.
Compare two versions of a song a few times, and Eigentone builds a preset from what you prefer.
Eigentone crashed recently. Nothing is sent unless you choose to.
Eigentone is off, so both will sound the same until it\'s on.
Manual: move a tone yourself, and mark peaks and dips
Lower means that ear needed a louder tone, as on an audiogram. This compares your ears with each other, and isn\'t a measure of how well you hear.
Is the new sound actually better than what you had? Switch between them, ideally on more than one song. Keeping what you had is a perfectly good answer.
Level in, left to right. Level out, bottom to top.
Nothing held up when checked twice, so there\'s nothing to add. Your headphones sound even to you, or the differences are too small to be worth fixing.
Nothing is playing. Start your music app to hear this, because Eigentone only changes its sound.
One point per line, such as 100 +4 or 1.6k -2. Copy the values from another app\'s EQ to match it. Levels between points are filled in.
Only save it to Your shapes
• Play a song you know well, and keep it playing.
• Set a comfortable volume, and leave it there.
Switch between them as often as you like while the music plays. Both are matched in loudness.
Switch between them while your music plays. They play at about the same loudness, so the louder one doesn\'t win just for being louder.
Switch instantly, with an optional blind test
That isn\'t a valid share code.
That\'s a lot of spots for a single pair of headphones, and some may just be how your ears hear different notes. Compare carefully, and run this again if the result sounds worse.
The sound goes back to Flat, and night mode, balance, ear correction and level settings are cleared. Your saved presets, hearing checks and output choices are kept.
The start and end are the same, so night mode won\'t turn on.
These narrow filters would even out what you noticed. Play some music and compare before keeping them.
This finds what you hear on these headphones. It isn\'t a measurement.
This is what you preferred with this music and these headphones. Other songs may suit it differently, and you can run the test again at any time.
This isn\'t a medical hearing test and can\'t diagnose anything. If you\'re worried about your hearing, see a professional.
This phone wouldn\'t play the tone.
Use less of it, or add bass or treble back
You\'ll compare two versions of your music a few times and choose the one you prefer. It takes about two minutes, and there are no wrong answers.
You\'ll hear quiet tones in one ear at a time and say whether you heard them. It takes about 3 minutes, and it makes a gentle curve that lifts what you hear least well.
You won\'t hear this while Eigentone is off or bypassed.
Your headphones may have their own EQ
The buttons are in a random order, and you\'ll find out which is which after you choose. Try more than one song.
Switch back and forth, ideally on more than one song.
The other one was %1$s. A single choice can be down to chance, so it\'s worth trying again if the two were close.
Night mode is on, so it\'s used instead.
The limiter is off, so a lot of makeup can distort.
Wear the headphones you want this for, and go somewhere quiet.
Turn on noise cancelling if you have it, and set the headphones\' own EQ to flat.
Set your usual music volume, and don\'t change it during the check.
Stop if a tone is ever uncomfortable.
This phone wouldn\'t play the tone. Try Play again.
This lifts the frequencies you heard least well, by half the difference. These headphones\' own tuning is part of the result, so it suits them best.
Your results were about even across frequencies, so there\'s no shared curve to add.

Your ears differed by up to %1$s dB at some frequencies, which can also come from fit. Eigentone can close half of that gap, frequency by frequency, with a separate EQ for each ear. It\'s saved for %2$s, and you can also do this later from the Sound tab, under Space.

You\'ll hear a note alternating with the notes just beside it, and say whether it stands out. There are about %1$s short questions, then a few more about anything you flagged. It takes around 3 minutes.
Keep your volume low, and stop if a tone is ever uncomfortable.
If you\'re unsure, answer Same. Only clear differences are worth fixing.
Does this note stand out from the ones beside it?
Checking again: does this note stand out from the ones beside it?
EQ in a headphone app, such as soundcore, Sony or Galaxy Wearable, adds to this one, so changes can apply twice. For the clearest results, set it to flat or default, and turn off any bass boost.
A correction evens out these headphones\' sound, using published measurements. You can undo it or turn it down at any time.
Play something to set up its preset.
Another audio app has control. Try closing or turning off: %1$s.
No filters yet. Add one to start shaping the sound.
Tap a point on the curve to edit it.
Android\'s own spatial audio is on, and adds to this. Try one at a time.
A separate EQ for each ear, for %1$s
For %1$s, from your hearing check on %2$s.
Ear correction is also saved for %1$s, and turns on when connected.
This preset\'s compressor is on, so it\'s used instead.
Loud music could reach %1$s, which can distort. Turn on the limiter, or lower the preamp or compressor makeup.
Loud music could reach %1$s. The limiter is holding it back, which can flatten peaks. Lowering the preamp or compressor makeup avoids that.
This preset uses faders or a curve, so use Export EQ file instead.
This phone only allowed %1$s bands, so narrow filters will be less accurate.
With earbuds, fit matters more than any setting. If bass sounds thin, try other ear tips before adding EQ.
EQ in a headphone app, such as soundcore, adds to this one. Set it to flat or default, or changes can apply twice.
Use one EQ at a time
It picks a correction for your headphones if one is known, then tunes it to what you prefer. It always checks the result against what you had.
A change of 2 or 3 dB is clearly audible. Very large boosts usually add distortion and lower the overall level.
Change a little at a time
If something is too loud, cutting it often sounds cleaner than boosting everything else.
Your ears adapt within minutes, so switch back and forth. If you can\'t hear a benefit, keep the simpler setting.
One track can mislead you. Test with a few you know well before settling on a sound.
Eigentone is off, so you won\'t hear this until it\'s on.
Bypass is on, so you won\'t hear this until it\'s off.
Tap the star on any shape to keep it here.
%1$s faders miss this shape by up to %2$s dB.
Compression curve. Levels above %1$s dB are reduced at %2$s to 1.
Now: %1$s. Your spot plays every other note. If it stands out from the notes beside it, mark it too loud. If it sinks below them, mark it too quiet.
Now: %1$s, your spot. Your spot plays every other note. If it stands out from the notes beside it, mark it too loud. If it sinks below them, mark it too quiet.
Equaliser curve. Use the filter controls below to adjust it.
Equaliser curves, with a separate curve for each ear.
%1$s band faders. Use the band controls below to change them one at a time.

resources.string: Which of these two notes is stronger?
Which of these two notes is weaker?
Where the bass change fades out. Low values affect only deep rumble, and higher values reach into punch and warmth.
A second bass setting kept from an earlier version, so this sound didn\'t change when the two bass controls became one. Set it to zero to remove it.
The correction as AutoEq published it.
As AutoEq published it, which aims for about %1$d dB less deep bass than Harman. If this sounds thin, try Harman.
The curve most listeners preferred in Harman\'s tests, at about 64%% of those tested.
About 2 dB less bass than Harman, which about 21%% of those tested preferred.
5 dB more bass than Harman. About 15%% of those tested preferred 4 to 6 dB more.
Harman\'s target with its bass lift taken out, for a leaner sound.
The older diffuse-field reference. Listeners in Harman\'s tests found it lean in bass and forward at 2 to 4 kHz.

A measured correction evens out your headphones towards a sound signature, and published ones don\'t all aim for the same bass. This moves it to the signature you choose. Harman\'s listening tests are where the figures come from, and they describe groups of people, so go by what you like. Targets are saved with the preset.
Sounds thin? Try the Harman target
This correction aims for less bass than most listeners preferred in Harman\'s tests. You can compare them on your music.
Device follows your phone\'s light or dark setting, including any schedule. Light suits bright places, and Dark suits low light. The sound isn\'t affected.
